title: Impact of Unemployment Benefit Eligibility on Future Earnings

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

**Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD)** is the appropriate causal method here. The setup is classic RDD:

- **Running variable**: `running_var` (age, normalized so the cutoff is at 0.5)
- **Cutoff**: Individuals above the age threshold (0.5) become eligible for unemployment benefits (`treated = 1`)
- **Outcome**: `y` (log earnings two years later)

**Key Assumption**: The **continuity assumption** — in the absence of treatment, potential outcomes would be continuous through the cutoff. Individuals cannot precisely manipulate their age to sort around the cutoff, which is inherently satisfied since age is not manipulable. This means any discontinuity in outcomes at the cutoff can be attributed causally to benefit eligibility.

I will estimate local linear regressions on both sides of the cutoff, use optimal bandwidth selection (Imbens-Kalyanaraman or CCT), and check robustness with different bandwidths, polynomial orders, and a McCrary density test for manipulation.

## 2. R Code

```r
# =============================================================
# RDD Analysis: Unemployment Benefit Eligibility on Earnings
# =============================================================

# Install packages if needed
for (pkg in c("rdrobust", "rddensity", "ggplot2")) {
  if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) install.packages(pkg)
}

library(rdrobust)
library(rddensity)
library(ggplot2)

# ----- Load Data -----
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s87_data.csv")
cat("=== Data Summary ===\n")
cat("N =", nrow(df), "\n")
cat("Treated:", sum(df$treated), "| Control:", sum(!df$treated), "\n")
summary(df)

# ----- Identify the cutoff -----
# From the data preview, treated=1 when running_var > ~0.5
cutoff <- 0.5
cat("\nAssumed cutoff:", cutoff, "\n")

# Verify treatment assignment
df$above <- as.integer(df$running_var >= cutoff)
cat("Treatment matches above-cutoff:", mean(df$treated == df$above), "\n\n")

# ----- 1. Main RDD Estimate (rdrobust with MSE-optimal bandwidth) -----
cat("============================================\n")
cat("  MAIN ANALYSIS: rdrobust (MSE-optimal BW)\n")
cat("============================================\n")
rd_main <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cutoff, 
                     kernel = "triangular", p = 1, bwselect = "mserd")
summary(rd_main)

tau_main <- rd_main$coef[1]  # Conventional estimate
se_main <- rd_main$se[1]
cat("\n>>> Main RDD Estimate (Conventional):", round(tau_main, 4), 
    "  SE:", round(se_main, 4), "\n")
cat(">>> Robust Bias-Corrected Estimate:", round(rd_main$coef[3], 4),
    "  SE:", round(rd_main$se[3], 4), "\n")
cat(">>> Robust 95% CI: [", round(rd_main$ci[3,1], 4), ",", 
    round(rd_main$ci[3,2], 4), "]\n")
cat(">>> Optimal bandwidth (h):", round(rd_main$bws[1,1], 4), "\n\n")

# ----- 2. Robustness: Different bandwidths -----
cat("============================================\n")
cat("  ROBUSTNESS: Varying Bandwidths\n")
cat("============================================\n")

h_opt <- rd_main$bws[1,1]
bandwidths <- c(h_opt * 0.5, h_opt * 0.75, h_opt, h_opt * 1.25, h_opt * 1.5)

bw_results <- data.frame(bandwidth = numeric(), estimate = numeric(), 
                          se = numeric(), pval = numeric(), nobs = numeric())
for (h in bandwidths) {
  rd_h <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cutoff, 
                    h = h, kernel = "triangular", p = 1)
  bw_results <- rbind(bw_results, data.frame(
    bandwidth = round(h, 4),
    estimate = round(rd_h$coef[1], 4),
    se = round(rd_h$se[1], 4),
    pval = round(rd_h$pv[1], 4),
    nobs = rd_h$N_h[1] + rd_h$N_h[2]
  ))
}
cat("Bandwidth sensitivity:\n")
print(bw_results, row.names = FALSE)

# ----- 3. Robustness: Higher-order polynomial (p=2) -----
cat("\n============================================\n")
cat("  ROBUSTNESS: Quadratic Local Polynomial\n")
cat("============================================\n")
rd_quad <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cutoff, 
                     kernel = "triangular", p = 2, bwselect = "mserd")
summary(rd_quad)
cat(">>> Quadratic RDD Estimate:", round(rd_quad$coef[1], 4), 
    "  SE:", round(rd_quad$se[1], 4), "\n\n")

# ----- 4. Robustness: Uniform kernel -----
cat("============================================\n")
cat("  ROBUSTNESS: Uniform Kernel\n")
cat("============================================\n")
rd_unif <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cutoff, 
                     kernel = "uniform", p = 1, bwselect = "mserd")
cat(">>> Uniform Kernel Estimate:", round(rd_unif$coef[1], 4), 
    "  SE:", round(rd_unif$se[1], 4), "\n\n")

# ----- 5. Simple parametric RDD (for comparison) -----
cat("============================================\n")
cat("  PARAMETRIC RDD (full sample, linear)\n")
cat("============================================\n")
df$X_centered <- df$running_var - cutoff
df$D <- as.integer(df$running_var >= cutoff)
param_model <- lm(y ~ D * X_centered, data = df)
cat("Parametric estimate:\n")
print(summary(param_model))
cat("\n>>> Parametric RDD Estimate:", round(coef(param_model)["D"], 4), "\n\n")

# Near-cutoff subsample
df_near <- df[df$near_cutoff == 1, ]
if (nrow(df_near) > 0 & nrow(df_near) < nrow(df)) {
  param_near <- lm(y ~ D * X_centered, data = df_near)
  cat(">>> Parametric (near cutoff only, N=", nrow(df_near), "):", 
      round(coef(param_near)["D"], 4), "\n\n")
}

# ----- 6. Manipulation Test (McCrary / rddensity) -----
cat("============================================\n")
cat("  MANIPULATION TEST (rddensity)\n")
cat("============================================\n")
density_test <- rddensity(X = df$running_var, c = cutoff)
summary(density_test)
cat(">>> Density test p-value:", round(density_test$test$p_jk, 4), "\n")
if (density_test$test$p_jk > 0.05) {
  cat("    -> No evidence of manipulation (good!)\n\n")
} else {
  cat("    -> Possible manipulation concern\n\n")
}

# ----- 7. RD Plot -----
cat("============================================\n")
cat("  GENERATING RD PLOT\n")
cat("============================================\n")
rdplot_out <- rdplot(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cutoff,
                      title = "RDD: Unemployment Benefit Eligibility on Log Earnings",
                      x.label = "Age (Running Variable)",
                      y.label = "Log Earnings (2 years later)",
                      binselect = "es")

# ----- Final Summary -----
cat("\n============================================\n")
cat("  FINAL SUMMARY\n")
cat("============================================\n")
cat("Main RDD estimate (conventional):", round(tau_main, 4), "\n")
cat("Main RDD estimate (bias-corrected):", round(rd_main$coef[2], 4), "\n")
cat("Main RDD estimate (robust):", round(rd_main$coef[3], 4), "\n")
cat("Robust p-value:", round(rd_main$pv[3], 4), "\n")
cat("Robust 95% CI: [", round(rd_main$ci[3,1], 4), ",", round(rd_main$ci[3,2], 4), "]\n")
cat("Optimal bandwidth:", round(h_opt, 4), "\n")
cat("Effective N (left + right):", rd_main$N_h[1], "+", rd_main$N_h[2], "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings

**Sign**: I expect a **positive** discontinuity at the cutoff, meaning that eligibility for unemployment benefits **increases** future earnings (log earnings two years later).

**Magnitude**: Based on the data preview — where treated observations (running_var > 0.5) show values like 0.48, 0.52 while untreated show values like 0.37, 0.12, 0.06 — I expect the RDD estimate to be approximately **0.2–0.4 log points** (i.e., a 20–50% earnings increase).

**Economic Rationale**: This positive effect is consistent with the theoretical literature on unemployment insurance as a search subsidy. Benefit eligibility provides a financial cushion that allows workers to:
1. **Search longer** for better job matches rather than accepting the first available position
2. **Invest in retraining** or skill development during the unemployment spell
3. **Match more efficiently**, resulting in higher-quality employment and higher wages

This aligns with findings in the literature (e.g., Nekoei & Weber, 2017) showing that more generous UI can improve post-unemployment match quality and earnings, particularly when measured at a 2-year horizon that captures the medium-term benefits of better matching.

**Robustness expectations**: The estimate should remain stable across bandwidth choices and polynomial orders. The McCrary density test should show no manipulation (age is not manipulable). The `near_cutoff` variable may serve as a pre-defined bandwidth indicator for local analysis.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: The cutoff age for benefit eligibility provides a natural experiment to assess causal impacts.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Eligibility for unemployment benefits at the cutoff age increases log earnings two years later.
